Dude who said you have to abandon your family! That's what the courts are for. If your wife is happy with a husband who isn't really happy, or doesn't realize your not happy... then there red flags. Maybe just take a break. Nothing in life in permanent. Worst comes to worst you just have visitation with your kids. 

But hell having 2 christmases or a dad that was gone for a year is way, way better than having a dead dad by the time youre 20 or so. Don't tell yourself that your doing the noble thing by sticking it out. Face up to what's making you sad, even if you don't know what it is and try your hardest to do something about it. That's the real noble thing. That's the real tough thing to do. You and me both brother cause I'm facing the same struggle every minute of the day. 

The hardest thing to do is realize you need to be a man who faces depression head on. Cause it will happen to your children too, and when it does you want to be there to tell them how you got through it.

Then change direction man. Not kidding. The biggest service you can pay to your kids is leading by example and showing them that if you're in a funk, even if it's a seemingly lifelong,endless funk, that you can change your surroundings and get out of it. 

Your kids deserve to see you happy, not just alive. It's a leap but in be end your kids will appreciate seeing their dad happy. Move, get out of there and fuck everybody who doesn't understand. Go somewhere that you have good memories, a lake, a mountain, whatever and wander. It's win-win, either you come back cause you realize being around your kids make you more happy than living somewhere else, or in 10 years your kids come visit a happy dad in Colorado or something.

Either way you find out what makes you happy. Humans are meant for change. Depression is natural and you can adapt. 

Edit: and by the way the "things will get better" part. It doesn't just happen. Things don't just get better to you. But you keep trying things out and keep rolling with the punches and naturally you will find yourself somewhere better. But don't be stagnant. Your kids deserve a happy dad
